title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Samir Gupta
description: Motivation: reduce unit economics for common inference workloads by shipping conservative autotuned defaults for batching and KV-caching, attach quantization profiles for recommended model variants, and expose unit-economics tooling to make tradeoffs visible to customers. Changes in this PR: 1) Autotune engine: add new "default_profiles" that produce conservative batching/caching settings derived from historical latency percentiles and SLOs; these defaults are the new fallback used when customers opt into 'autotune: recommended' in route config. 2) Batching defaults: introduce max_batch_size cap heuristics, adaptive request grouping thresholds, and improved backpressure handling to avoid latency spikes under bursty traffic. 3) KV-caching defaults: enable prefix caching by default for reunionable routes and add TTL heuristics to reduce memory churn. 4) Quantization profiles: add a profiles YAML catalog with recommended quant levels per model family and attach compatibility metadata (expected token perf impact, supported hardware). 5) Unit economics tooling: CLI and API to estimate per-token cost/latency tradeoffs given traffic shape and selected profile; adds a small internal UI export for Console. 6) Tests and benchmarks: integration harness updates and new benchmark job to validate cost regressions and SLO adherence. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind "autotune_recommended_defaults". Gradual rollout to dedicated clusters for 2 weeks with nightly benchmark runs and alerting on 99p latency regressions > 10%. Related: ENG-1023, ENG-1187. Checklist: - [x] Autotune default policy implementation - [x] Batching/caching runtime hooks - [x] Quant profile catalog added - [x] UEcon CLI + API endpoints - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Benchmarks added - [x] Docs updated (console + release notes) Notes: kept defaults intentionally biased toward latency SLO preservation at the expense of some batching throughput to avoid regressions reported in recent incidents. This is intended as a conservative, observable default; further autotune iterations will relax thresholds once we collect more rollout telemetry.
